summary.headline: Uniparts Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR347 crore and EBITDA 55% to INR90 crore, with management guiding FY27 growth a few points above FY26's 21%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR347 crore (+27% YoY), with EBITDA of INR90 crore (+55% YoY, +10% QoQ) and PAT of INR57 crore (+64% YoY, +11% QoQ). Management said the quarter was in line with its quarterly guidance and above its annual guidance. Construction equipment is now 45% of revenue and drove growth, while large ag is at its cyclical trough and growth there comes from new wins. Aftermarket was flat YoY in absolute terms but fell to about 12% of revenue as OEM business grew faster. Net cash is about INR190 crore and the company is debt-free, with about half a dozen acquisition targets under review.

segments.name: Construction equipment
segments.commentary: Now 45% of total revenue and the main growth driver in Q1 FY27; momentum that began in 2H CY2025 has continued, supported by US and European infrastructure spend.

segments.name: Large agricultural equipment
segments.commentary: Conditions subdued; management expects about a 15-16% decline in CY2026 after about 30% in CY2025. Growth is from new wins, particularly in Europe, not market recovery.

segments.name: Small agricultural equipment
segments.commentary: India performing well on government subsidies and mid-to-high HP adoption, with strong new wins. Western small ag still soft but volumes have started recovering after three years of decline.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: About 12% of Q1 FY27 revenue (vs 15% in FY26 and 20% in FY25), flat YoY in absolute terms; tariff-driven price volatility deferred channel purchases.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth to be a couple of percentage points above FY26's 21% growth, per management; Q2 FY27 expected to be in line with Q1.
Management expects FY27 EBITDA margin comfortably above 20%; long-run cycle margin guidance remains about 20% (peak to trough).
Second half expected to be better than first half, linked to the ag recovery.
Mexico facility: first customer deliveries from the warehouse expected in Q3 FY27; FY27 Mexico revenue in mid-single-digit USD million.
Warehouse sales expected to stay in a 52-56% range over the next 12-18 months.
Material cost range of 34-37% of revenue is considered sustainable; fabrication vertical expected to become meaningful in 18-24 months.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex of INR12 crore; organic capex (fresh equipment plus repairs and maintenance) guided at 2.5-3.5% of revenue.
Fabrication facility for small and medium-sized fabrication set up about 2.5 years ago; now in deep discussions with OEMs to supply fabrications.
Restoration of the Ludhiana finishing shop is on schedule; customer supply uninterrupted.
Mexico operations on track; Phase 2 may add manufacturing in Mexico.
demand_pricing: Channel mix: warehouse sales about 56% of Q1 FY27 revenue (vs 50-52% in Q1 FY26); locally made and locally sold about 22% (vs about 25%); the balance is direct exports.
Margin hierarchy by channel: locally made and sold is lowest; direct exports are the base (about 20% margin); warehouse sales are highest.
Product margins stated as broadly similar across three-point linkage, precision machined parts and fabrication; material consumption differs by product mix.
New business order book over INR225 crore on a trailing 12-month basis; new wins split roughly equally between Europe and US, with the majority of wins in ag and construction.
Above-70 HP three-point linkage is a single-digit market share with a major European OEM win in FY26; below-70 HP is dominant share globally.

qa_highlights.question: Will the construction share of revenue structurally rise and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said construction is 45% of revenue; drivers (new wins, industry recovery, wallet expansion) are multi-quarter. Mix will rebalance as ag recovers.

qa_highlights.question: Is construction higher margin than tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Product margins are fairly similar; differences come from channel. Warehouse sales are highest margin, direct exports about 20% base, and locally made/sold lowest.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on acquisitions and their revenue timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About a dozen targets evaluated since IPO in hydraulics, fabrication and PTO; about half a dozen currently under close review. Targets must be ROCE/ROE accretive within 18-30 months, manageable, and not deeply distressed.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the 33.3% material cost and the gross margin level?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly product mix (three-point linkage, precision machined parts, fabrication have different material consumption), plus channel mix; inventory gain only about INR1 crore. Material cost range 34-37% is typical.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the aftermarket?
qa_highlights.answer: Flat in absolute terms YoY; demand deferred by tariffs and inflation. Management expects normalisation over the next 12 months as tariffs have come down.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to gain share in large ag?
qa_highlights.answer: Share is lower due to OEM validation and testing cycles; FY26 wins are now flowing into P&L, and deep discussions are ongoing on several opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2.5-3.5% capex guidance inclusive of acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It covers organic capex (fresh equipment and R&M). Acquisitions would use the INR190 crore cash and could involve debt; the balance sheet is strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 expected to be in line with Q1 and robust; H2 expected to be better than H1, tied to the ag recovery.

risks_watch: Large ag remains at cyclical trough in CY2026 (about 15-16% decline expected); recovery is only expected through CY2027.
Western small ag recovery is early and consumer buying for big-ticket items remains deferred due to economic uncertainty.
Aftermarket softness: tariffs and West Asia-driven inflation; management expects normalisation over the next 12 months.
Input cost and supply chain pressure from the West Asia situation.
Margin sensitivity to warehouse sales mix, currency movements and industry recovery pace.
Acquisition execution: no deal yet despite about a dozen targets evaluated since IPO; timing and value accretion uncertain.
Mexico warehouse ramp: first deliveries expected Q3 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: About 25% in Q1 FY27; about 24% in Q4 FY26 (as stated on call)
33.3% of revenue (includes about INR1 crore inventory gain)

key_quotes: The new business momentum is structural, and we intend to build on it.
Our growth in this segment is therefore not market-driven. It is entirely the result of new business wins, with particular momentum in Europe.
The truth of the matter is that we have evaluated about a dozen targets since IPO across hydraulic fabrication and PTO.
So Q2 looks very robust, and I think Q2 should be in line with Q1.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and balance sheet, with a clear recovery narrative for construction and small ag. Cautious on large ag, which management says is at its trough, and on aftermarket, which it says was deferred by tariffs and inflation. Evasive on acquisition specifics, declining to name targets or give revenue timing.

adds.what: Mexico warehouse: first customer deliveries expected; Phase 2 may add manufacturing in Mexico
Fabrication facility for small and medium fabrication (set up ~2.5 years ago), now moving to supply fabrications to OEMs

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth a couple of points above FY26's 21% (about 23%), Q2 in line with Q1 at ~INR347 crore, and H2 better than H1; Mexico first deliveries in Q3 FY27 add modest growth, but large ag is still declining 15-16% in CY2026 and capacity additions are small.
